title: Constraint and Assumption
definition: A constraint limits an acceptable solution, while an assumption is a condition treated as true until evidence confirms or invalidates it.
purpose: Make mandatory boundaries and uncertain beliefs independently reviewable.
history: Engineering requirements processes distinguish imposed constraints from assumptions that require monitoring and validation.
mental_model: A constraint is a wall around acceptable solutions; an assumption is a labeled bridge that must be inspected before trusting it.
analogy: A locked venue closing time is a constraint, while expecting all guests to arrive early is an assumption; organizational authority determines which rules are truly mandatory.
common_mistakes: Presenting a preference as a constraint
Presenting an assumption as a fact
industry_notes: Visible assumptions support risk management, change impact analysis, and safer design decisions.
ai_notes: AI often turns common patterns into unstated assumptions; engineers must label and verify them.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to classify several project statements as constraint, assumption, preference, or open question.
lab_candidates: Create an assumption ledger with owners and invalidation impact
project_candidates: Record constraints and assumptions for the project contract
